citation: Hernández Albarracín, Juan Diego; Álvarez González, Carlos Fernando; Pallarès Piquer, Marc. "Heidegger y la fenomenología de la existencia: una analítica cinematográfica del aburrimiento en la modernidad" [Heidegger and the Phenomenology of Existence: A Cinematographic Analytic of Boredom in Modern Times]. Tópicos, Revista de Filosofía, no. 62 (enero-abril 2022): 193-222. Universidad Panamericana. https://doi.org/10.21555/top.v62i0.1624. NOTE: manifest's provisional single-author label ('Hernández Albarracín') and short title ('Cinematographic Analytic of Boredom') are CONFIRMED but INCOMPLETE, not incorrect -- verified against the source's own title page; three co-authors, bilingual dual title.
thesis: Heidegger's three forms of boredom (Langeweile) and their two structural modes (Hingehaltenheit/being-held-in-limbo, Leergelassenheit/being-left-empty), developed in the 1929-30 Freiburg lectures (FCM), can be interwoven with narrative-film readings so that cinema becomes a hermeneutic-phenomenological vehicle for diagnosing modernity; boredom's essence (aburribilidad/Langweiligkeit) is the fundamental mood (Grundstimmung) of the present era, symptomatically fled through a technological/entertainment culture that estranges Dasein from encounter, questioning, and self-care.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.summary: Grounds Langeweile in Being and Time's Befindlichkeit; rejects causal-psychological readings of mood via Wittgenstein's 'world of the happy/unhappy' and Heidegger's anti-'mere tint' thesis.

sections.title: Historical brief (Breviario histórico-conceptual del aburrimiento)
sections.summary: Genealogy of boredom's marginalization in Western thought: acedia, Burton's melancholy, Enlightenment duty/Kant, Huysmans, Pascal, Kierkegaard (via Svendsen), Romantic literary ennui, Durkheim.

sections.title: First form: 'aburrimiento por...'
sections.summary: Read through Van Sant's My Own Private Idaho (1991) and Tarkovsky's The Killers (1956, after Hemingway): waiting, clock-checking, failed Zeitvertreib.

sections.title: Second form: 'aburrimiento en...'
sections.summary: Read through Huston's The Dead (1987, after Joyce) and Bergman's Hour of the Wolf (1968): pastime collapsing into the occasion itself; Unheimlichkeit; extended present.

sections.title: Third form: 'uno se aburre' / profound boredom + kairological excursus
sections.summary: Read through Visconti's White Nights (1957, after Dostoevsky): no pastime possible, total refusal of beings; followed by an excursus on the Augenblick (Being and Time §45) against chronological time.

sections.title: Technology/modernity coda (Ocupación de sí y relaciones tecnológicas)
sections.summary: Heidegger's technology critique; the 'technological overflow' (desbordamiento tecnológico) thesis (citing co-author Álvarez González's own 2018 dissertation); brief gestures at science-fiction cinema (Alphaville, Blade Runner, Terminator, Matrix, A.I., I, Robot); Méndez's 'metaontology.'

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.summary: The three forms are horizontally co-present, not hierarchically staged; boredom opens onto the question of Being; gestures toward future work on solitude/finitude via Vattimo.

constructs.label: being-bored-by (1st form)
constructs.treatment: the 'most everyday and recognizable' form; staged as waiting-for-an-event (empty road, bar clock-watch)

constructs.label: being-bored-with (2nd form)
constructs.treatment: the pastime becomes indistinguishable from the situation itself; produces an extended, self-enclosed present

constructs.label: profound/deep boredom (FCM 3rd form)
constructs.treatment: 'es ist einem langweilig' staged as an anonymous Sunday stroll with no pastime available; total refusal of beings-as-a-whole

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: implicitly refused as a frame -- aburribilidad is ontological-structural, not a diagnosable internal state/trait caused by an external stimulus

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: connective construct across all three forms: Zeitvertreib as 'driving time along'; clock-checking as symptom of failed pastime; kairological Augenblick vs. chronological time

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: modern technological/entertainment culture diagnosed as producing meaninglessness while marketing itself as escape from boredom

constructs.label: flow/engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: negative instance only -- the Bergman dinner-party 'pastime' itself relapses into boredom rather than escaping it

constructs.label: boredom-as-regulatory-signal (functional account)
constructs.treatment: explicitly contested -- rejects the causal-psychological 'diagnose and measure the neurosis' model of mood

constructs.label: mind-wandering / task-unrelated thought
constructs.treatment: present only as phenomenal description (looking 'toward nothing in particular'), not thematized in cognitive-science terms

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: present only as phenomenal description (the White Nights stroller's diffuse, unseen observation), not thematized

readings.claim: Boredom (Langeweile) is a Grundstimmung, not a psychological state produced by an external cause and awaiting clinical diagnosis; moods regulate not only the one who has them but all in contact with them.
The first form's Hingehaltenheit/Leergelassenheit is legible in narrative cinema as repeated clock-checking and failed pastime.
The second form's pastime does not repel time but is coextensive with the situation itself, producing an Unheimlichkeit beneath an outwardly pleasant occasion.

The third form's 'es ist einem langweilig' opens onto kairological, ecstatic time (the Augenblick of Being and Time §45) rather than chronological time, demanding Dasein shoulder its existence rather than disperse into das Man.

Modern technological/entertainment culture has 'overflowed' (desbordamiento tecnológico) the entire horizon of Dasein's possibilities, foreclosing authentic care (Sorge) even as choices multiply within that horizon.
The three forms of boredom are horizontally co-present modalities of Dasein-world relation, not hierarchically/developmentally staged from shallow to deep.
The boredom produced by technological overflow might itself be the route back to authentic self-relation.

interlocutors.role: primary phenomenological source for the three forms and their structural modes

interlocutors.name: Heidegger, Martin — Being and Time (Ser y tiempo)
interlocutors.role: background architecture: Befindlichkeit, das Man, the Augenblick (§45), fleeing-from-self

interlocutors.name: Svendsen, Lars — Filosofía del tedio
interlocutors.role: genealogy of tedium (Kierkegaard), transparency/extremity, clock-watching-as-failure motif

interlocutors.name: Escudero, Jesús Adrián
interlocutors.role: on affects stigmatized since Plato/Descartes; epochal Grundstimmung claim

interlocutors.name: Löwith, Karl
interlocutors.role: on resolute selfhood ('que el hombre se acuerde de sí mismo') vs. das Man

interlocutors.name: Held, Klaus
interlocutors.role: Grundstimmung as disclosing historical totality; Dasein's Seinkönnen

interlocutors.name: Foucault, Michel
interlocutors.role: 'cuidado de sí' (self-care) register, via the Rux Martin interview

interlocutors.name: Wittgenstein, Ludwig — Tractatus
interlocutors.role: 'world of the happy/unhappy' as relational analogue for mood-constituted worldhood

interlocutors.name: Vattimo, Gianni
interlocutors.role: closing frame: Heidegger 'polarized' between individual experience and belonging-to-world-as-totality

interlocutors.name: Mendieta Rodríguez, E.
interlocutors.role: companion analysis of chronic ennui in cinema (La grande bellezza); anonymous-bored-observer motif

interlocutors.name: Hernández Albarracín, Juan Diego (self-citation)
interlocutors.role: co-author's own prior work on Langeweile and poetry (Pizarnik, 2012) and on Heidegger-to-Morin complexity (2016)

interlocutors.name: Álvarez González, Carlos Fernando (self-citation)
interlocutors.role: co-author's own 2018 doctoral dissertation on autonomous weapons systems, source of the 'desbordamiento tecnológico' concept

tensions.axis: phenomenological-ontological Grundstimmung vs. scientistic/clinical-causal account of mood
tensions.note: the source firmly rejects the causal-diagnostic model; this is the same debate axis grounding bor-sec-25/bor-sec-26 (Elpidorou's regulatory-functional account) on the opposing side.

tensions.axis: hierarchical/developmental reading of the three forms (shallow-to-deep) vs. horizontal/co-present reading
tensions.note: the article explicitly rejects a staged/escalating reading in its conclusion, insisting the three forms are equally available modalities rather than steps toward profundity.

following Heidegger's own critique of the Aristotelian metaphorá schema (FCM §21), the source implicitly treats film images as disclosive rather than as vehicles onto which mood is merely transferred -- a methodological commitment never made fully explicit.
